## Core conclusion

The current specification (2026-07-28) frames stdio as one UTF-8 JSON-RPC message per line: messages are newline-delimited and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines. Servers read stdin and write protocol messages to stdout. Servers MUST NOT write non-MCP content or JSON-RPC requests to stdout. Servers MAY write UTF-8 logging strings to stderr, including informational, debug, and error messages. Clients MAY capture, forward, or ignore stderr and SHOULD NOT assume stderr output indicates an error.

## Main recommendations

These recommendations are proposals based on the research, not validated outcomes.

- Keep banners, debug prints, and other logs off stdout; send logging to stderr instead.

## Limits to keep in mind

- The prohibition on server JSON-RPC requests applies to the cited current revision; do not automatically apply it to older protocol versions.

Source verification: model-reported (byte-level source verification is not performed).
